thread:
maria: quick sync — thinking about a small RFC follow-up: we should separate burst credits from sustained credits at the admission layer.
ben: can you clarify why both? we've already got reservoir buckets and soft-credits.
maria: short answer: abuse surface and tail latency. bursts are fine if bounded; sustained noisy tenants mess with fairness. separating windows gives better degradation controls.
kevin: hmm, so two pools per tenant? one short-window(?) and one long-window? 
sara: yeah, that sounds like the classic leaky-bucket + reservoir combo. what's the tradeoff for admission plumbing?
maria: plumbing: minimal change if we treat the short window as a pre-admission fast-path (cheap check) and the long window as the real fairness allocator. Pre-admit rejects reduce path amplification.
ben: example flow?
maria: sketch: client hits edge -> fast check against burst_pool (1s window, small tokens) -> if pass, go through normal routing. if fail, hit long_pool check (60s window) that may allow slower throughput or probabilistic admission.
kevin: probabilistic admission = use p = min(1, long_pool_tokens / demand) ?
sara: avoid using raw demand in policy; attackers spoof rps. prefer token-gain rates and decayed usage.
infra-bot: deploy note: will need new telemetry: pacing.check_fast, pacing.check_long, pacing.reject_fast, pacing.reject_long, pacing.probabilistic_sample.
alex: what headers / API would we expose for operator visibility?
maria: propose X-RW-PACING: burst=10/1s; steady=600/60s; mode=probabilistic or strict. Operators can tune per-tenant.
ben: nice. sample header: 
```
X-RW-PACING: burst_tokens=10;burst_window=1s;steady_tokens=600;steady_window=60s;mode=probabilistic
```
kevin: implementation notes: keep admission-memory tiny. store (last_refill, tokens) for short_pool; long_pool can be sharded into epoch buckets to avoid hot keys.
sara: migration path? we can't flip on for all tenants.
maria: rollout: 1) opt-in flag per tenant in config; 2) default-off global; 3) enable for a handful of noisy tenants; 4) run canary w/ 10% traffic; 5) monitor latency, rejections, and user errors.
ben: what about fairness interactions with existing scheduler (weighted fair queue)?
maria: scheduler should consume from long_pool only. fast-path passes straight into queue but still decrements long_pool asynchronously to keep accounting eventually consistent. That avoids priority inversion.
kevin: sketch of eventual-consistency: fast-debit ledger entry appended, reconciler subtracts from long_pool each minute. risk: short-term oversubscribe — but that's okay for small bursts.
sara: sounds ok. need guardrails to prevent gameable behavior — e.g., very short requests to keep using bursts.
maria: mitigate via burst_decay: consecutive_burst_count increases effective token cost, or require X-RW-CLIENT-ID header; also detect rapid short-tail patterns and convert to probab reject.
infra-bot: ops checklist: add metrics (burst_usage, steady_usage, fast_reject_rate, long_reject_rate), alert if burst_usage > 70% for 5m and long_reject_rate > 1%.
alex: telemetry event names?
maria: pacing.fast.allow, pacing.fast.reject, pacing.long.allow, pacing.long.reject, pacing.long.sampled_allow. All should include tenant_id, route, model_tag, token_cost_estimate.
ben: tests: unit tests for refill logic, chaos test with synthetic client that flips pattern (5x short then long). e2e: verify no net fairness regression vs current system.
kevin: compatibility: default credit balancing script needs to be updated to split historical usage into both pools during migration. if missing, long_pool should backfill from historical average.
sara: any security concerns? attackers might try to force reconciler failure to inflate available long_pool. need reconciler idempotency and signed ledger entries.
maria: agree — ledger entries should be HMAC'd per instance and reconcile only idempotent ops.
alex: can we do a small PoC in staging? I'll volunteer my team for the canary.
maria: thanks — want a short RFC doc? I'll write a 1-pager with config examples, rollout playbook, metrics, and observable dashboards. aiming to ship PoC in 2 weeks.
ben: SGTM. add me and kevin as reviewers.
sara: add QA and SRE for chaos tests.
kevin: adding a note: make sure the admission code sits in a single shared lib with a clear interface so private deployments can tune windows without changing platform logic.
maria: yep — API boundary: Admission.check(tenant_id, request_metadata) -> Decision{allow, reason, tokens_used, sampled}. Keep it language-agnostic and small.
infra-bot: reminder: this thread will be archived automatically in 90d.
maria: thanks all — I'll drop the 1-pager link when ready. :rocket:
